nodes.label: websocket() route directive
nodes.rationale: Server-side WebSocket is part of the HTTP route DSL: websocket() produces a Route, so it composes with path(), concat() and withMiddleware(), and upgrades matching requests onto a single hub actor. Works on all three backends via @fastify/websocket, ws, or Hono's per-runtime helpers.

nodes.label: WebsocketServerActor
nodes.rationale: One hub actor per route sees every connection's events, serialized. Type parameters read from the server's point of view: TOut is what the server sends, TIn what it receives. Helpers are this.connection, reply, broadcast (optionally filtered), clients and closeAll.

nodes.label: Internal per-connection actor
nodes.rationale: onReceive is sealed on a WebsocketServerActor: for every connection the framework spawns an internal connection actor as a child of the server actor, which owns the socket, decodes inbound frames, writes outbound and is stopped when the socket closes. Every event for a connection is ordered onClientConnected -> onMessage* (frame order) -> exactly one onClientDisconnected, so the actor model's no-concurrent-handler guarantee holds without locks.

nodes.label: WebsocketConnection
nodes.rationale: Extends ActorRef<TOut> with id, remoteAddress, upgrade info, isOpen, tell (encode via codec), sendRaw (bypass the codec) and close. It is a ref but cannot be deathwatched - onClientDisconnected is the single ordered end-of-life signal per connection.

nodes.label: maxFrameBytes
nodes.rationale: Checked twice: in the transport at bind time (a frame over it is refused while it arrives, so the client sees an abnormal 1006 close rather than 1009) and in the connection actor on the fully received frame before decode (closing with 1009). Only the second layer is a guarantee - the transport cap is an optimisation that spares the process the buffering. A server has one shared transport, so where routes disagree the transport takes the widest cap while each route's actor still enforces its own.

nodes.label: Runtime pairs with no transport frame cap
nodes.rationale: Two pairs buffer the frame before rejecting it: Deno, whose upgradeWebSocket exposes no payload limit at all, and Bun with the Express or Fastify backend, where the ws specifier resolves to Bun's built-in shim which accepts maxPayload and reads it back unchanged while enforcing nothing - measured, a 2 MiB frame against a 1 MiB cap reached the handler intact where Node refused it at the socket. The guarantee holds (the frame never reaches your actor) but the memory is spent first, so put a proxy with its own frame limit in front of an internet-facing endpoint on those pairs.

nodes.label: allowedOrigins (CSWSH defence)
nodes.rationale: Browsers attach the user's cookies to a WebSocket upgrade automatically, so a route whose auth is ambient (a session cookie, or IpAllowlist) is open to Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking. allowedOrigins gates the handshake by the Origin header, rejecting an unlisted origin with 403 before the handshake on all three backends. A missing Origin is allowed because CSWSH is a browser-only attack, and BearerTokenAuth is already resistant since browsers cannot set Authorization on a WS handshake.

nodes.label: Middleware runs at upgrade time
nodes.rationale: withMiddleware composes with websocket() but runs once against the HTTP upgrade request, not per message, so auth middleware gates the handshake. The underlying framework's own middleware runs too - Fastify route hooks, Express and Hono app.use - and the framework's guard runs after all of them, so withMiddleware and allowedOrigins always have the last word. Prefer withMiddleware for cross-backend identical behaviour, native middleware to reuse an existing ecosystem.

nodes.label: rawCodec / jsonCodec
nodes.rationale: The route codec decodes inbound frames into TIn and encodes TOut replies; jsonCodec is the default and accepts a validate hook, rawCodec hands over raw frames for binary protocols. Decode failures throw WebsocketDecodeError and follow the route's onInvalidMessage policy - close (1003), drop, or route to the actor's hook.

nodes.label: WebSocket backpressure policy
nodes.rationale: When a client cannot keep up its send buffer grows; past maxBufferedBytes (4 MiB default) the connection either drops frames (default) or is closed. Broadcasts to many slow clients are where this bites, so the policy has to match the protocol. Route defaults resolve as route options > HOCON (actor-ts.http.websocket) > built-in defaults, resolved at bind so a malformed value errors at bind() rather than on the first upgrade.
